preheader: Anthropic preps for IPO, Nvidia launches RTX Spark chips, and social security sees a bump.

lead.headline: Anthropic hits $16.8 billion in quarterly revenue as it prepares to go public
lead.body: The AI company behind Claude reported massive financial growth ahead of its anticipated initial public offering. Prospective investors were told the firm generated positive free cash flow alongside an 85% adjusted gross margin in the third quarter.
lead.why: This is a blueprint for how massive AI startups scale into profitable enterprises. Keep an eye on its valuation multiples and margins for your upcoming finance and valuation classes.

stories.headline: Memory chip stocks face severe sell-off as oversupply and yield issues mount
stories.body: Major manufacturers like SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron are taking a beating in the latest tech slide. Industry experts point to manufacturing yield complications, where half of certain architectural chips are ending up in the bin due to defects.
stories.why: Understanding how hardware supply chains and manufacturing yields impact public tech equities is vital for both your investing portfolio and any tech sector consulting prep.

stories.headline: Social Security benefits will increase by 3.6% in 2027
stories.body: The Social Security Administration announced its largest cost-of-living adjustment since 2023, driven by a year of high inflation. The adjustment will affect more than 72 million Americans starting next year.
stories.why: Tracking how inflation adjustments flow through government programs helps you map broader macroeconomic trends and consumer purchasing power.

stories.headline: Nvidia officially launches its RTX Spark PC platform built on MediaTek silicon
stories.body: Nvidia is rolling out a new class of Windows PCs featuring custom 18 and 20-core chips with up to 128GB of unified memory. Major creative software like Adobe Photoshop and Premiere has been entirely rearchitected to run on the new hardware.
stories.why: This marks a major shift in personal computing hardware as chipmakers chase local AI performance. Watch how hardware bundling affects enterprise software pricing models.

stories.headline: Amazon-owned Bee unveils new personal AI wearables starting at $75
stories.body: Bee introduced its first product lineup since being acquired by Amazon last year, including an updated wearable and a credit-card-sized recorder. The devices integrate with Alexa to summarize conversations and manage to-do lists.
stories.why: Consumer hardware startups face massive distribution hurdles, making Amazon's acquisition playbook a great case study for your entrepreneurship classes.

stories.headline: McKinsey integrates AI client avatars into its entry-level interview process
stories.body: Candidates applying to McKinsey now have to conduct a 10-minute conversation with an AI-generated client avatar during in-office interviews. Human observers watch how applicants listen and respond to the virtual client's business concerns.
stories.why: Since you are interested in consulting, note how top firms are using generative AI to test human soft skills and structured problem-solving under pressure.

stories.headline: Newport Beach finance leaders bring 'Fearless Girl' replica to UC Irvine
stories.body: A life-size replica of the bronze statue that stands opposite the New York Stock Exchange was displayed at UC Irvine for an event hosted by Women Investing in Security and Education.

stories.headline: Jessica Pegula's Wuhan Open match interrupted by fan seeking an autograph
stories.body: A spectator approached Jessica Pegula mid-match with a hat and marker while she was discussing tactics with her coach during a medical timeout against Jelena Ostapenko.

term.name: Convertible Note
term.definition: A form of short-term debt that startup founders use to raise early-stage money without having to set a formal company valuation right away. The loan automatically converts into equity later when the startup hits a major milestone or raises a priced financing round. Today's news highlights how popular this instrument remains for early fundraising.

serve.headline: Abby Care raised $82 million to turn family members into paid caregivers
serve.body: Transformation Capital and CVS Health Ventures backed the health tech startup as it tackles the severe shortage of professional care specialists. The fresh capital will help expand its platform connecting families with structured compensation models.
questions: How does a healthcare startup scale operations when its labor force consists of everyday family members rather than certified professionals?
What customer acquisition channels make the most sense when selling a caregiving platform to health systems and insurers?
If you were pitching CVS Health Ventures on this deal, what unit economic metrics would you highlight first?
